newsitem.title: USA: Judge lifts stay for Marvel bondholders.
newsitem.headline: Judge lifts stay for Marvel bondholders.

text.p: In a victory for Marvel Entertainment Inc. bondholders, a federal bankruptcy judge Tuesday lifted a stay that prevented them from trying to foreclose on common stock backing the the New York-based comic book and trading card company's bonds.

U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Helen Balick's ruling gives bondholders -- who have been fighting majority investor Ronald Perelman's Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization plan -- the right to foreclose on the stock "without limitations," said bondholders' attorney David Friedman.
The bondholders will now consider whether to exercise that right, Friedman said.

"We've been granted the opportunity to vote ... but we hope that won't be necessary," Friedman said. "We hope to sit down with the Marvel board and convince them that that the current plan on file is not in the best interest of any party."
Marvel spokesman Michael Freitag said the company will review the available legal options, including an appeal or request for a temporary restraining order.
Balick said arguments presented by Marvel's parent company against the bondholders' request were without merit.

Perelman's reorganization plan would reimburse the bondholders 4.5 cents on the dollar in exchange for their collateral stock, which dropped 12.5 cents Tuesday to $1.875 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Bondholders have been fighting the plan.

Perelman's plan is based on a series of deals that begin with a $365 million stock investment in Marvel from his wholly owned Andrews Group Inc. The money would be earmarked to buy Toy Biz Inc. stock not already owned by Marvel.
Perelman would then control 80 percent of new Marvel stock, while bondholders' collateral would be diluted from 78.8 percent to 17.2 percent.
